pr_comments:
The problem with this change is that is it valid to proceed if the memcpy is protected?

Should special handling be taken in that case that the non protected path gets taken or should we just throw an exception or trigger an assert?

> The problem with this change is that is it valid to proceed if the memcpy is protected?
> 
> Should special handling be taken in that case that the non protected path gets taken or should we just throw an exception or trigger an assert?

The main issue with the relevant code lies in the assumption that when `count` is 0, `memcpy(dest, src, count)` will do nothing, hence `dest` or `src` can be NULL. However, even if `count` is 0, having `dest` or `src` as NULL constitutes undefined behavior (#25819 has more specific explaination).

Therefore, I think that protect the `memcpy` function can eliminate this undefined behavior while maintaining its original semantics.
Please remove the unnecessary "[Merge branch 'xbmc:master' into master](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/25820/commits/73abb79eaea52f759d42228d000db18a6e947411)" commit.

> The end result looks now good 👍
> 
> What's not so nice are the commits, they are not structured properly. Please clean them up with one meaningful change per commit.

I'm not very familiar with git. Could you please help me check if the new commit complies with the standards? Thank you!

<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
#### Some reference about `memcpy(dest, src, count)`

According to https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/string/byte/memcpy, if either `dest` or `src` is an invalid or null pointer, the behavior is undefined, even if count is zero.

And there is an [example](https://godbolt.org/z/aKWhsMrbb) shows how this UB affect program's behavior after `gcc -O3` optimization. 
<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->
<!--- A bug report that is not clear will be closed -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->



## Expected Behavior
Eliminating this kind of UB.
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->



## Actual Behavior
<!--- Tell us what happens instead -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->

### xbmc-xrandr.c
After returning from `init_transform` at line 1240, `&crtcs[c].current_transform`'s field `nparams` is 0, `params` is NULL. Then `&crtcs[c].current_transform` is passed as 2nd parameter of `copy_transform` at line 1242.

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/741f0604fddf1a33aca00c88f6d148f3723c62e9/xbmc-xrandr.c#L1238-L1242
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/741f0604fddf1a33aca00c88f6d148f3723c62e9/xbmc-xrandr.c#L582-L591

Entering `copy_transform`, parameter `src` correspond to `&crtcs[c].current_transform`, so `src->params` is NULL, `src->nparams` is 0.

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/741f0604fddf1a33aca00c88f6d148f3723c62e9/xbmc-xrandr.c#L603-L606

Then `memcpy(dest->params, NULL, 0)` at line 600 is undefined behavior.

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/741f0604fddf1a33aca00c88f6d148f3723c62e9/xbmc-xrandr.c#L593-L601

### xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/DVDDemuxers/DVDDemuxCC.cpp
If `data.size()` is 0, `pPacket->pData` is initialized as NULL, then there is a UB at line 488.

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/741f0604fddf1a33aca00c88f6d148f3723c62e9/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/DVDDemuxers/DVDDemuxCC.cpp#L486-L488

### lib/libUPnP/Neptune/Source/Core/NptUtils.cpp
At line 370, if `separator` is NULL, `separator_length` is set to 0, then there is a UB at line 380.

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/741f0604fddf1a33aca00c88f6d148f3723c62e9/lib/libUPnP/Neptune/Source/Core/NptUtils.cpp#L370-L383


## Possible Fix
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix or reason for the bug -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Check `count` before invoking `memcpy`.
